blocks: In chant and polyphony the E mode was hard to cadence in, because no leading tone rises to the final. Renaissance cadences in the E mode pair F–E in the bass with D–E above it. Heard from A minor, the result sounds like a half cadence.

That cadence outlived the mode. The Baroque "Phrygian half cadence", iv6–V in minor, uses the same half-step bass descent to the dominant. The two-chord Adagio of Person/Johann Sebastian Bach's Brandenburg Concerto No. 3 is one.
Flamenco's characteristic sound is usually Phrygian with a major tonic, close to the fifth mode of Music/Scale/Minor/Harmonic, over the Andalusian cadence i–♭VII–♭VI–V.
Heavy metal leans on the ♭2 for darkness, often as a riff that alternates the tonic with ♭II.
In jazz chord-scale theory it fits a minor seventh chord functioning as iii, and the sus4♭9 chord voiced over it.
Carnatic music's Hanumatodi, melakarta 8, is this collection. See Music/Scale/Todi for the different Hindustani Todi.
It is the inversion of the major scale: the major step pattern read downward from the tonic gives Phrygian.
Phrygian and Locrian are the only diatonic modes with a ♭2. The ♭II triad sits a half step above a minor tonic, the relation the Neapolitan chord borrows in common-practice minor.
The tonic has no dominant: the triad on 5 is diminished (G B♭ D♭).
In sargam: S r g M' P d N. On C: C D♭ E♭ F♯ G A♭ B. Steps in semitones: 1 2 3 1 1 3 1.
One of Person/Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande's ten Hindustani thaats, named for raga Todi. See Music/Scale/Marwa for how a thaat relates to the ragas inside it.
The principal raga is Miyan ki Todi. Its name ties it to Miyan Tansen, the singer at Akbar's court in the sixteenth century.
The Carnatic equivalent parent scale is Shubhapantuvarali, melakarta 45.
Miyan ki Todi is a late-morning raga. Pa is weak or skipped in ascent, and the lowered Re, Ga and Dha are sung slightly flat of their equal-tempered pitches, with slow oscillation.
Gujari Todi drops Pa entirely; Bilaskhani Todi takes its notes from the Bhairavi thaat yet keeps the Todi name.
The name points to two different scales. Carnatic Todi, Hanumatodi or melakarta 8, has the notes of Music/Scale/Phrygian, while Hindustani Todi has a raised fourth and a raised seventh.
Its step pattern, 1 2 3 1 1 3 1, contains two augmented seconds, like Music/Scale/Minor/Hungarian, from which it differs only in the second degree.
Also Person/Olivier Messiaen's first mode of limited transposition. On C: C D E F♯ G♯ A♯. Steps in semitones: 2 2 2 2 2 2.
Glinka used a descending whole-tone scale for the sorcerer Chernomor in Ruslan and Lyudmila (18/4/2), and Russian composers after him kept it for the supernatural.
Person/Claude Debussy made it a harmonic field. "Voiles" (Préludes, Book I, 1909–1910) stays on one whole-tone collection for most of its length and turns pentatonic in the middle.
Messiaen listed it first among his modes of limited transposition in Technique de mon langage musical (1944), and said he avoided it because Debussy and Dukas had used it so thoroughly.
Impressionist harmony, and later film and television, use it for dreams, flashbacks and suspended time.
Jazz uses it over a dominant seventh chord with a ♯5 and 9 (C7♯5, C9♯5), and Person/Thelonious Monk made descending whole-tone runs a signature.
